Instrumental drifts are real but independent: each apparatus has its own physical drift source (thermal, mechanical, optical alignment, sensor aging) uncorrelated with the others. Weak cross-correlations reflect genuine instrumental isolation.

All drifts are noise, no real instrumental shift: the observed z-scores are consistent with sampling variation from stable underlying means. Cross-instrument agreement is weak because there is no true signal to correlate.

Systematic calibration drift in a shared measurement standard or reference (e.g., clock, frequency source, environmental sensor used to correct all instruments) produces correlated drift in all four channels, but the correlation is obscured by large uncorrelated instrumental noise floors.
Non-stationary baseline: the first 10 days (baseline period) were not in true steady state. The apparent post-baseline drift is a regression to a more stable mean, not an instrumental drift.

Environmental transient or intervention occurred around Day 26, affecting pendulum_lab trial 242 (event 688928: 1.6948 beats, +1.57% excursion), signaling a genuine physical or instrumental perturbation on that day that other instruments either missed or did not express visibly.
